issues.evidence: Line 2 ends with the CJK full stop '。' instead of the Devanagari danda; the Tibetan line 'རྣམ་པར་དཔྱད་ན་ཆུ་ཤིང་འདྲ། །' is otherwise rendered correctly.

Tibetan 'འཚེ' (Sanskrit upadrava) is harm/affliction generally; bo-kunpal 9-159 glosses it as 'ཕྱི་ནང་གི་ཉེར་འཚེ་སྣ་ཚོགས' (various outer and inner troubles) and bo-shenga as being harmed by others. 'हिंसा' (violence) narrows it.

issues.span: जैसे कोई बार-बार स्नान, / करके बार-बार अग्नि में प्रवेश करते हैं
issues.evidence: Tibetan 'འགའ་ཞིག' ('some', plural) with 'ཡང་ཡང་ཁྲུས། བྱས་ཏེ་ཡང་ཡང་མེར་འཇུག་པ' (bathing again and again, then entering fire again and again). Hindi has singular 'कोई' with plural verbs 'करते हैं/मानते हैं' and a stray comma splitting 'स्नान' from 'करके'.
